title: Global Dam Watch (GDW) Database of River Barriers and Reservoirs v1.0
description: The Global Dam Watch consensus database (v1.0) harmonises earlier global dam datasets — including GRanD, GOODD and dams derived from the JRC Global Surface Water dataset — into 41,145 georeferenced river barriers (points) and 35,295 associated reservoir polygons, with attributes such as dam name, river, year, height, reservoir area and storage capacity, main use and a quality index. It supersedes the Global Reservoir and Dam database (GRanD).
purpose: Provides an open, harmonised inventory of Algerian dams and reservoir outlines (location, capacity, year, use) to link reservoir-based water supply with surface-water, drought and hydrological basin data.

spatial_extent.description: Global inventory; 88 barriers have COUNTRY = 'Algeria' (from GRanD 50, GOODD 25, JRC-GSW 13), located in the Tell, High Plateaux and Saharan Atlas basins (e.g. Beni Haroun, Koudiat Acerdoune, Taksebt, Gargar, Djorf Torba). Users filter the attribute table by country.

temporal_extent.description: Static v1.0 inventory (figshare record created 2024-07-25). Dam construction years for Algerian entries range from 1932 to 2021; dams commissioned after the compilation are missing. A removal-year field is included.

variables.name: MAIN_USE / USE_*
variables.description: Main and secondary uses (irrigation, supply, hydropower, flood control, ...)

variables.name: QUALITY
variables.description: Quality index (Verified, Good, Fair, Poor, Unreliable)

variables.name: ORIG_SRC / POLY_SRC
variables.description: Original source of the record and of the reservoir polygon

processing: Records from multiple global and regional datasets were consolidated, de-duplicated and manually inspected; locations were co-registered to HydroSHEDS/RiverATLAS and reservoir polygons to HydroLAKES v1.1 (for Algerian records the POLY_SRC field lists SWBD for 51, JRC-GSW for 32 plus 1 modified, and McGill for 4). A generic quality indicator was assigned to each record.
validation: The Technical Documentation (section 2.9) describes uncertainty handling and a five-level quality flag; no quantitative accuracy statistic is given for attributes.
limitations: Not a time series: it gives capacity and outline, not reservoir filling or water level.

Algerian coverage (88 barriers) may be incomplete relative to the national dam inventory, especially for recent dams and small hill reservoirs (retenues collinaires); it could not be compared with ANBT data, whose website was unreachable.
Attributes such as capacity or year may come from secondary sources and can differ from official Algerian figures; check the QUALITY and source fields.
Reservoir polygons are static outlines from specific source dates and do not reflect current filling levels or siltation.
Download is through a request form on the GDW website or the figshare record; the authors ask that the full dataset not be re-hosted without permission.

algeria_notes: The 88 Algerian records total about 9,370 million m3 of reported storage capacity (sum of CAP_MCM in GDW v1.0, not an official figure). Use GDW to locate dams and outline reservoirs, then combine with JRC Global Surface Water or Sentinel-2 to monitor water extent over time; reservoir filling rates are published nationally (ANBT) but could not be accessed for this check.

unverified_fields: completeness relative to the Algerian national dam inventory
verification.notes: The shapefile package was downloaded from figshare and the barrier attribute table filtered on COUNTRY = 'Algeria' to count records (88), sources, capacities and years. The figshare landing page returns HTTP 202 to scripted requests (bot protection), so the record was verified through the figshare API and DataCite; the DOI URL is listed for access. GRanD was not given a separate record because the GDW site states that GRanD 'is now superseded by the GDW database'. DAHITI (reservoir water levels) was considered but Algerian targets could not be confirmed without registration.
